decided_by: team-lead, 2026-08-25, after the correction scope was re-derived and two of the three originally-agreed edits were withdrawn
headline: Three sites assert mpralegnet is a 'candidate'. All three are CORRECT and must not be 'fixed'. Two of them are working drift guards. An audit that reads the terminal disposition and then harmonises these sites would replace a true label with a false one and disable both guards.

why_this_record_exists.the_near_miss: The correction that produced this record was originally scoped to rewrite the roster status and the admitted_task. Both were endorsed before the site inventory was re-derived. Neither is a defect. Had they been applied, the campaign would have traded a true label and two guards for a false one.
why_this_record_exists.the_general_trap: A terminal disposition creates pressure to harmonise every nearby field to match it. Fields that look inconsistent with a block are not automatically wrong: a model can be simultaneously a roster candidate, admission-blocked, and terminally blocked from scoring, because those three statements are made by three different layers about three different questions.
why_this_record_exists.instruction_to_future_auditors: Do not edit the three sites below to agree with terminal_disposition_20260825.json. If you believe one of them is wrong, read this record first and then raise it, rather than editing.

non_changes.why_it_stays: The defect is PROVENANCE EQUIVALENCE, not terms. The only roster value that reads as blocked is 'blocked_terms', and it would be actively false: the licence is MIT code and MIT weights, and the terms are not what failed. No roster status value expresses 'terminally blocked on provenance'. 'candidate' plus admission_blocking = true is the closest honest encoding the schema permits, and the precise reason lives in the terminal disposition.
non_changes.additional_reason: This file is the frozen base registry. The campaign rule is that registry changes are additive versioned overlays leaving the frozen base byte-identical.
non_changes.what_breaks_if_changed: Both guards below, plus the byte-identical-base invariant.

non_changes.why_it_stays: This is not an assertion that mpralegnet is scorable. It is a guard that fails if the roster identity moves. It encodes no falsehood. Editing it to say something other than 'candidate' would silently disable detection of an unauthorised roster edit.
non_changes.note: This is the same shape as the scGPT lesson but with the opposite conclusion. There, a test asserted sha256 == UNRESOLVED and encoded a real falsehood, so the test had to change with the bundle. Here the guarded value is true, so the guard stays. The test to change is the one encoding a false fact, not every test that mentions the model.

non_changes.why_it_stays: Second independent runtime guard keyed to the same roster value. It raises if the roster status or exposure moves without authorisation.
non_changes.discovery_note: This site was named by neither the team-lead nor the first-pass audit. It was found only by grepping source and scripts for the model id rather than reasoning about which files 'ought' to assert status. A three-site inventory derived from expectation missed it; a six-site inventory derived from grep found it.

sites_that_are_defects_and_are_handled_e.blocker: The file is hash-pinned by config/gse281364_comparator_reconciliation.toml [file_authorities.mpralegnet_checkpoints] and by config/local_variant_family_reconciliation.json file_authorities.mpralegnet_checkpoints. Editing it makes both stale, so both must be refreshed in the same transaction. The literal digest is deliberately NOT reproduced here -- see phantom_pin_note.
sites_that_are_defects_and_are_handled_e.companion_fields_checked: Both pin records carry only path + sha256 for this file. No size_bytes, count or date companion describes it, so the 'a pin is rarely one field' trap does not apply to this particular refresh. Verified on the reconciled tree at 16:45, not assumed.

sites_that_are_defects_and_are_handled_e.blocker: The capability record schema is closed at eight keys, allowed_endpoints rejects empty, and the validator requires the capability model set to equal the roster's variant_to_regulation models. No in-schema edit can express a scoring block. Escalated as C1/C2/C3.
sites_that_are_defects_and_are_handled_e.ruling: User ruling via team-lead, 2026-08-25: extend the schema (C1). Not the base-roster route (C3), and not accepting the split (C2). Sequenced after the pin-refresh lane's branches B and D land.
sites_that_are_defects_and_are_handled_e.scope_requirement: Must be the GENERAL fix, not an mpralegnet patch. Any model registered for variant_to_regulation and later terminally blocked hits the same three walls, so a field only mpralegnet can use would leave the next blocked model exactly here.
sites_that_are_defects_and_are_handled_e.enforceability_requirement: The new field must be consulted by the gate, not merely declared. The defect being corrected is precisely that scoring_authorized:false in a disposition file never reached the layer that gates scoring; a v2 field no evaluator reads would rebuild that defect one level up. The proving test must call the gate directly rather than assert on config.

verification.asserts: All three non-changed sites still hold their recorded values, so an unauthorised harmonisation fails a test instead of landing silently.

known_unenforceable_block.statement: Between this record and C1 landing, mpralegnet is BLOCKED ON PAPER AND SCORABLE IN PRACTICE. This is a known unenforceable block, not a resolved item.
known_unenforceable_block.why: terminal_disposition_20260825.json sets scoring_authorized=false, but config/evaluation/variant_to_regulation_capabilities.toml still grants models[mpralegnet].allowed_endpoints = [allelic_direction, mpra_activity], and that capability registry is what an evaluator consults. The disposition layer and the gating layer disagree, and the gating layer wins at runtime.
known_unenforceable_block.do_not_read_this_record_as_closure: If you are reading this and concluding the gate holds, it does not. Check whether C1 has landed before relying on the block.
known_unenforceable_block.pending_work: C1 schema extension, sequenced after refresh branches B and D.
known_unenforceable_block.interim_control: Manual. Do not schedule mpralegnet on variant_to_regulation on either allowed endpoint until C1 lands.

v1_consumers_to_move_at_v2.enumerated_on: 2026-08-25, before any edit, per team-lead instruction
v1_consumers_to_move_at_v2.non_obvious_consumer: tests/unit/_sealed_fixtures.py CONSTRUCTS a v1 capability document rather than only reading one, so a v2 bump must move the fixture builder as well as the validator. A grep for the consumer path alone would have missed that it is also a producer.

phantom_pin_note.defect: An earlier draft of this record reproduced the mpralegnet checkpoints.json digest as a literal, to explain the blocker. That made this record appear -- to any digest grep, and plausibly to the pin contract test -- to be a THIRD pinner of a file it only describes.
phantom_pin_note.why_it_matters: It would have gone stale the moment sites A and C landed, manufacturing a dead pin out of a prose sentence, in a record whose entire subject is not manufacturing false assertions.
phantom_pin_note.fix: The blocker now names the two pinning records and their table keys without reproducing the digest.
phantom_pin_note.generalisation: A record that quotes a digest to talk ABOUT a pin is indistinguishable, to a grep, from a record that HOLDS a pin. Descriptive prose in an audit record should name the pinning file and key, not echo the hash.
phantom_pin_note.self_caught: Found by re-deriving my own pin inventory on the reconciled tree, per the team-lead instruction not to trust an inventory built before a concurrent write. The re-derivation returned pinned_by=3 where I expected 2.
